newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico authorities retract on prosecutor arrest.
newsitem.headline: Mexico authorities retract on prosecutor arrest.

text.p: The Mexican government on Thursday retracted an official report and said that a former prosecutor had not been formally arrested.
A spokesman for the attorney general's office, who earlier had confirmed to Reuters the arrest of ex-prosecutor Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, said the information he had given was incorrect.

"Mr. Chapa Bezanilla is definitely not under arrest," the spokesman said. "We must apologise, unfortunately ... because it was confirmed to us and so I took the liberty of saying he had been officially arrested."
He declined to say what Chapa's situation was, but said authorities had been seeking him under an order to testify about allegations of bribery and body snatching, not under an arrest warrant.
Chapas is a former special prosecutor who led several major assassination probes. He ordered the arrest in 1995 of ex-president Carlos Salinas's brother Raul for murder.
Chapa has been on the run for three weeks after receiving the order to testify, saying he feared for his well-being.
Earlier on Thursday two government officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Chapa had been arrested in the central town of Jiutepec.

Chapa's sister Maria de los Angeles Chapa told Reuters she had spoken to Chapa's wife, who said his lawyers had told her he was not under arrest. "The family denies the information given by the attorney general's office," she said.
Chapa has said he was willing to turn himself in to authorities voluntarily if human rights observers were present to ensure he was treated correctly.
It was not clear if he was now voluntarily helping police with their enquiries, or if he was still on the run.

Chapa was fired from his job as special prosecutor at the attorney general's office in December following a bizarre turn in his probe of the September 1994 murder of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, a top leader of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Chapa was in charge of the exhumation of a skeleton at a ranch used by Raul Salinas that investigators claimed was the body of a missing legislator wanted in the Ruiz murder.
Authorities believed that the legislator had helped Raul Salinas plan the murder and was then killed to silence him.
Raul Salinas is in jail awaiting a judge's verdict on his case and denies any involvement in the Ruiz killing.
The body at the ranch turned out to be someone else's, planted by a witch who was helping Chapa with the probe.

The witch, known as "La Paca," is under arrest on body snatching charges following revelations that the body belonged to a dead relative whom she and other family members had dug up from a local cemetery and reburied at the ranch.
Chapa was also wanted to testify on allegations that he made illegal payments to witnesses in the case.
